expectedTruths: Population (standardised common factors): PQ = 0.45 CE; PV = 0.15 CE + 0.55 PQ; SAT = 0.10 CE + 0.45 PQ + 0.35 PV; LOY = 0.65 SAT (the ACSI structural pattern without the complaints construct). R^2 — PQ 0.202500, PV 0.399250, SAT 0.597838, LOY 0.422500.
All items are on a 1-10 scale (model.json scale {min: 1, max: 10}); IPMA performance uses these ORIGINAL endpoints, never the observed extrema.

Thresholds are shifted per construct (PQ -1.0, SAT -0.8, CE -0.6, LOY -0.5, PV -0.2), so PQ items have the highest and PV items the lowest performance: in an IPMA of LOY, PV combines a positive importance with the lowest performance.

IPMA importance is the UNSTANDARDISED total effect on 0-100 rescaled construct scores estimated from the sample; it is compared engine-to-engine, not to the standardised population effects (whose signs, all positive, are expected to agree).
These are NOT ACSI data: the structure is inspired by Fornell et al. (1996); the numbers come from this generator.
